claims.text: The proposed predictive approach explicitly incorporates multiscale modeling of local force-constant fluctuations and lattice distortions.
High mixing or configurational entropy produces pronounced local lattice distortions in high-entropy alloys.
Force-constant fluctuations in FeCoCrMnNi are approximately 20%.
Lattice distortions and force-constant fluctuations enhance scattering of heat-carrying phonons in high-entropy alloys.
Lattice distortion can reduce phonon velocity.
Enhanced phonon scattering caused by high-entropy lattice disorder lowers lattice thermal conductivity.
Explicitly modeling force-constant fluctuations and lattice distortions will identify low-phonon-thermal-conductivity high-entropy alloys more accurately than conventional methods.
Standard DFT-based or simplified theoretical models do not account for detailed force-constant fluctuations.
Conventional predictive models underrepresent phonon-scattering effects in highly disordered alloys.
The proposed approach will provide more precise estimates of reduced phonon mean free paths.
The proposed approach will predict lattice thermal conductivities in an ultralow regime near 0.4 W m^-1 K^-1 for suitable materials.
The proposed approach will reduce prediction error by approximately 10–20% relative to conventional methods.
The approach is primarily applicable to single-phase high-entropy alloys having enough configurational entropy to generate significant lattice distortion.
The approach may not be valid for multiphase or segregated alloys because phase boundaries or other extrinsic factors dominate their disorder effects.
The improvement in predictive accuracy will vary with alloy composition and experimental conditions.
Measured phonon-scattering behavior should correlate with predicted force-constant fluctuations and lattice distortions.
